note: Definitions used by this analysis, with links from first uses. Alternative meanings and unresolved distinctions are identified without selecting an approach.

terms.site_usage: One technical requirement or recommendation, finer-grained than a control, without any claim about whether it is binding. A working definition for comparing approaches, not selecting an interpretation.

other_usages.usage: A normative requirement, a shall, equivalent to a control
A statement of how a component may be configured, descriptive rather than binding

other_usages.who: Ambiguous usage; this analysis distinguishes rule from check

other_usages.usage: An AWS Config rule: a deployable resource with parameters

terms.site_usage: An executable or procedural test that determines whether a rule is satisfied. One rule may have many checks, one per tool.
The configuration prescribed by a rule, distinct from the system's observed configuration, or actual state.

other_usages.usage: Possible state: a technology provider describes available configurations rather than required configurations

terms.site_usage: The system's observed configuration, distinct from the configuration prescribed by a rule, or desired state.
A requirement from a regulatory framework, such as NIST SP 800-53. Coarser than a rule. One control is typically served by many rules.
An optional relationship from a rule to regulatory controls. A rule may serve several controls, one, or none. A rule without a control link can have observations but no control-targeted finding.
A published set of technology-specific hardening guidance, including CIS Benchmarks, DISA STIGs, CISA SCuBA baselines and technology provider guides.
Technology-specific guidance for configuring hardware, software or services securely. Used as a synonym for benchmark in this analysis.

Whether a statement is a shall, should or may. OSCAL has no dedicated core requirement-level field across these approaches. Properties can carry such labels, but consumers need shared conventions to interpret them; model placement alone does not establish requirement level.
Whether an artifact expresses binding requirements against which an auditor can assess a system. Normativity is part of the debate over model placement.

A Component Definition construct grouping components and control-implementations to express joint satisfaction. Whether capabilities should be added to the SSP or removed from Component Definition remains an open design question in this analysis. No position is selected.
Two distinct meanings are used: a component running checks, or a component describing validation against frameworks. This analysis identifies the intended meaning.

other_usages.usage: A component whose purpose is to run checks rather than to be checked. Type validation, carrying a checks array.
A component enumerating the compliance frameworks a service has been validated against.
other_usages.who: Alternative interpretation, not demonstrated by the OSCAL examples

terms.site_usage: An OSCAL assessment-assets element that may reference components through uses-components. The examples do not establish a consistent convention for distinguishing assessment platforms, assessment assets and components in runner descriptions.
terms.not_established_note: The open question is when a component alone identifies a runner and when an assessment platform adds necessary execution context.

terms.site_usage: The OSCAL assessment-assets container holds components and assessment-platforms. The examples do not establish a consistent convention for identifying runners across these structures.
terms.not_established_note: A consumer still needs to associate each task or observation with the asset used.

terms.site_usage: A part of a system, with related meanings across Component Definition, SSP, Assessment Plan and Assessment Results models. The distinction from assessment platforms and assets remains unresolved, as does granularity: a component may represent a configuration rule or a policy engine.
terms.not_established_note: The examples leave open whether components should represent individual rules, products or policy engines and how consumers reconcile those levels.

terms.site_usage: The tool or person performing a check, addressed by question 5. Actor is a neutral label in this analysis because no single OSCAL construct covers all uses.

other_usages.usage: An assessment platform, optionally reaching components through uses-components
A component of type validation, carrying the checks it runs
An origin actor on an assessment result
A tool named in a prop at task level
other_usages.who: The assessment plans in two of the three corpora

terms.not_established_note: The examples use different runner-identification conventions. No single convention is established here for associating a task or observation with its producer.

terms.site_usage: The system owner's narrative assertion of control implementation and design intent per component. The SSP represents claims through implemented-requirement, statement and by-component. Addressed by question 6a.

The assessor's evidence-based record of whether a control was satisfied for a subject at a point in time. The AR uses observation, finding and status for binary or graded outcomes. Addressed by question 6b.
An AR element recording observed evidence. Requires uuid, description, methods and collected, with no control reference. Observations are available for rules with or without control links.

An AR element recording whether an objective is satisfied. The required target type is restricted to statement-id or objective-id, both control-derived. A rule without a control link cannot have a finding.

An OSCAL model, GA since 1.2, relating collections of controls. Third parties can publish mappings after the source catalogs. The mapping-item type permits control and statement targets, not component rules or activities.
OSCAL model, Control layer. A structured set of controls and control enhancements.
OSCAL model, Control layer. A baseline or overlay that selects and customizes controls from catalogs.
OSCAL model, Implementation layer. Describes how components implement controls.
OSCAL model, Implementation layer. Documents how a particular system implements required controls. Abbreviated SSP.
OSCAL model, Assessment layer. Defines how controls will be assessed, through activities, steps and tasks. Abbreviated AP or SAP.
An assessment plan local-definitions element containing steps. How to divide a benchmark procedure between activities and steps remains an analysis question.
A child of an assessment plan activity. The examples do not establish one consistent boundary between the work represented by an activity and its steps.
OSCAL model, Assessment layer. Documents the results of control assessments, as observations and findings. Abbreviated AR or SAR.
OSCAL model, Assessment layer. Documents remediation plans for identified issues. Abbreviated POA&M.
One of three stakeholder roles. Publishes requirements or recommendations for organisations to version, tailor and cite without depending on a specific system.
One of three stakeholder roles. Uses requirements as desired-state configuration that a configuration engine can apply.
One of three stakeholder roles. Runs checks or reviews sufficient evidence to determine whether requirements are satisfied.
